decisions.reason: As a newly launched component that fits the firm's engineering-led, customizable drainage portfolio, there is no clear evidence of performance below aspiration and a mature firm would usually allow more time for market learning.

A floor-level shower drainage system sits directly in the firm's strategic core of accessible, low-profile bathroom drainage, so management would retain it absent clear signs of serious underperformance.

The designer shower drainage product supports the firm's design-conscious positioning and likely broadens appeal to architects and planners, so boundedly rational management would continue it while results are still uncertain.
The shower element with integrated slope strengthens the installation-ease proposition and complements existing system offerings, making retention the likely choice in the first post-launch period.

This backflow-protected basement floor drain solves a concrete technical problem and was given strong launch emphasis, so management would keep it while assessing whether it meets aspirations over a longer horizon.

Although less prominently presented, the air-admittance valve is still related to the firm's drainage know-how and a firm with some organizational slack would usually not drop such a recent product without clearer negative feedback.
